blog.title: Notes on agent memory
blog.subtitle: Bitemporal graphs, retrieval, and the lifecycle of a fact — how Brain works and why it's built this way.

hero.title: Memory with context.
hero.subtitle: Give your agent a memory across conversations. Brain connects facts, events and their sources, tracks what changes, and retrieves the evidence behind an answer. Connect over MCP or REST. Run it on your infrastructure or ours.

panel.title: A change, with its source
panel.label: Illustrative memory trace
panel.question: Which database did we choose?
panel.quote: “We moved to SurrealDB to keep graph relations and time-aware facts together.”
panel.note: Follow the decision back to the conversation that explains it.

bitemporal.title: A change has two dates.
bitemporal.subtitle: Acme changed plans on March 10. Brain learned about it on March 12. Move each clock to explore the difference between when something happened and when it was recorded.
bitemporal.validLabel: valid time — when it was true
bitemporal.scenario: Illustrative local demo · Acme plan change · no API request

notes.unknown: The transaction clock sits before Mar 12. Brain hasn't recorded the switch yet, so it still answers starter — even for dates after Mar 10. That's the past, replayed exactly.
notes.past: Valid time is before Mar 10. Back then, starter was the truth.
notes.current: Both clocks are current — the switch happened and Brain knows it. Growth is the live answer.

retrieval.title: Find the evidence. Then answer.
retrieval.subtitle: Hybrid search finds relevant memory. Graph retrieval follows known entities and relationships. Synthesis brings the evidence together and checks support for the answer.
retrieval.note: Retrieval and reranking stages are configurable. For a known entity, start with graph_retrieve; for a question spanning relationships, use search_multi_hop.

stages.name: Find relevant memory
stages.desc: Semantic and lexical search find candidates across the enabled memory layers.

stages.name: Follow relationships
stages.desc: Entity anchors and graph edges add related facts; multi-hop returns an auditable evidence chain.

stages.name: Rank in context
stages.desc: Time, relevance and source signals help select the evidence to pass to the model.

stages.name: Cite and verify
stages.desc: Synthesis cites its evidence. Strict guardrails can return no answer when support is insufficient.

dualPath.title: Two ways to run it. Same graph.

selfHost.label: Open source
selfHost.title: Self-host
selfHost.desc: Run Brain with Docker Compose, configure your model providers and keep control of deployment, storage and access.
bullets: LLM and reranking providers are configurable
Admin tools and evaluation harnesses included

managed.label: Managed
managed.title: brain.inite.ai
managed.desc: Connect to the hosted service with your organization account. Manage keys and explore memory through the web app.
bullets: No servers, no database to keep alive
Health and Prometheus metrics built in

stats.title: Quality needs a protocol.
stats.subtitle: Retrieval scores and answer accuracy measure different things. Read results alongside the dataset, model, baseline and run configuration.

items.label: Representation
items.floor: Does memory help when the transcript fits in context?

items.label: Capacity
items.floor: Can the system find answers across long conversation histories?

items.label: Scale
items.floor: How does quality change as the history grows?

stats.footnote: Strict binary judge · own full-context baseline · paired statistics · held-out split. Published results describe their recorded runs, not a guarantee for every deployment.

features.title: Facts change, and the memory has to change with them.
features.subtitle: From architecture decisions to customer conversations: the controls to keep memory useful as new information arrives.

items.title: Conflicts stay visible
items.desc: Updates can supersede earlier facts. Close calls stay COMPETING, with a dry-run tool to inspect the proposed resolution.

items.title: One entity, across mentions
items.desc: Aliases and canonical names help resolve repeated mentions, including code identifiers, to the same entity.

items.title: Remember why it was built
items.desc: Record architecture decisions and their rationale. Recall past choices with why and recall_decisions when the code changes.

items.title: Memory for your domain
items.desc: Packs define vocabulary and memory models: scene schemas, state transitions, verification and retention hints. Six industry packs ship in the repository.

items.title: Documents become memory
items.desc: Ingest a document through Source → Indexer → Candidates. Use one fact write for one claim, and the document pipeline for longer material.

items.title: Tools that match your access
items.desc: Read, write and admin scopes shape the available tools. Installed packs can extend the surface with operator consent.

items.title: Company and personal memory
items.desc: Tenants have separate databases. Pass userId for personal memory; omitting it selects tenant-global memory.

items.title: Retract or forget
items.desc: Retraction preserves an audit trail. Administrative forget hard-deletes an entity and its associated records, leaving tombstones.

quickstart.title: Connect once. Recall across sessions.
quickstart.subtitle: An API key is the only thing to paste — the workspace comes from the key. Connect an MCP client, call REST directly, or use the TypeScript SDK.
quickstart.copyError: Copy failed. Select and copy the code below.

mcpBlock.title: Your agent gets the right tools.
mcpBlock.subtitle: Native Streamable HTTP: one URL, one header, the workspace resolved from the key. One command in Claude Code or Gemini CLI, one click in Cursor and VS Code, and @inite/brain-mcp for harnesses that cannot send a header. Available tools depend on key scopes, enabled features and installed packs.
mcpBlock.clients: For personal memory, pass userId. For longer material, prefer ingest_document over recording a paragraph as one fact.

connectBlock.title: One click where one click exists.
connectBlock.subtitle: Cursor and VS Code publish an install URL, so those are buttons. The rest install from one command or one URL — handed over verbatim rather than behind a button that would only open a settings page.
connectBlock.keyHint: Every path needs an API key —

notes.claude-code: Installs the MCP server, the six skills and the lifecycle hooks together. Claude Code asks for the key and keeps it in the OS keychain.
notes.cursor: Opens Cursor and adds the server. Replace the placeholder key in its MCP settings.
notes.vscode: Opens VS Code and adds the server to the workspace. Replace the placeholder key when prompted.
notes.gemini: Installs the extension: MCP server, skills, and the agent guide as context. Export BRAIN_API_KEY first.
notes.claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, paste this URL. OAuth runs itself; there is nothing else to fill in.
notes.chatgpt: Add as a custom connector. This URL serves exactly the search + fetch pair ChatGPT requires — the default surface would be refused.

skillsBlock.title: Having the tools is not knowing when to call them.
skillsBlock.subtitle: Install workflows for search, recall, temporal queries, writes and conflict resolution. SKILL.md is a cross-agent format, so the same six work unchanged everywhere — the one-liner finds every agent on the machine and installs into each.
skillsBlock.targetLabel: shell · installs into every agent it finds
skillsBlock.targets: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, openclaw and opencode by autodetect; Cursor and the vendor-neutral .agents/skills with --scope project. Claude Code users can take the plugin instead and get the skills, the MCP server and the hooks in one command.

openSource.title: Built in the open, licensed AGPL-3.0.
openSource.subtitle: Read the code, run your own, send a PR. Everything that runs brain.inite.ai lives in the repo.

license.note: Network copyleft — self-host freely; changes you serve over a network stay open.

cta.title: Star the repo
cta.desc: Watch releases, open issues, send patches. The roadmap is public.

footer.tagline: Open-source memory for AI agents. Facts, context and sources, connected.

bitemporal.title: Bitemporal model
bitemporal.description: Two time axes per fact. asOf semantics with Allen-interval examples.

predicates.title: Predicate vocabulary
predicates.description: Single-active vs bitemporal vs append-only. Decay, PII class, v1.1 content predicates.

conflict-resolution.title: Conflict resolution
conflict-resolution.description: Scoring formula, COMPETING / SUPERSEDED / REJECTED outcomes, dead-letter.

ingest.description: Structured fact ingest, NLU mention extraction, typed edges.

multi-hop.title: POST /v1/search/multi-hop
multi-hop.description: Planner LLM decomposes the query, joint-F1 evaluable supporting facts.

retract.title: POST /v1/facts/:id/retract
retract.description: Mark a fact retracted. Survives in audit trail with reason.

domain-packs.title: Domain Packs
domain-packs.description: Versioned ontology plugins — manifest, signing, registry, marketplace.

document-pipeline.title: Document pipeline
document-pipeline.description: Source → Indexer → Candidates → Brain. Re-indexing, corroboration, privacy dials.

external-indexers.title: External indexers
external-indexers.description: The pull work API — poll, claim, read, submit. HMAC push hints, per-pack keys.

memory-files.title: Memory files
memory-files.description: File-shaped memory — the storage behind Anthropic's memory tool.

mcp-setup.title: MCP setup
mcp-setup.description: Claude Code, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Goose, n8n configs.

mcp-hooks.title: Lifecycle hooks
mcp-hooks.description: Recall at session start, capture before compaction — memory without asking the model.

skills.title: Skills bundle
skills.description: Six Anthropic-format skills, install.sh, versioning model.

operator-playbook.title: Operator playbook
operator-playbook.description: Day-2 ops — keys, scopes, process roles, dreams cron, baseline diffs.

security.title: Security model
security.description: JWT, scopes, ABAC policies, per-tenant isolation, GDPR forget, PII gating.

leases.title: Leases & claims
leases.subtitle: Leader-election + active job_run claims across the fleet. Use this to spot stuck workers, dead leases that haven't been re-acquired, or pods holding more than their share.

queueModeTip.enqueue: crons enqueue rows; worker loop dispatches
queueModeTip.inline: kill switch active — crons run inline (pre-Phase-J behaviour)

leases.poolTip: JobWorkerPool — node:worker_threads pool for cpuBound handlers (currently no handler opts in; size=0 disables the pool)

leaderLeases.title: Leader leases
leaderLeases.subtitle: Named locks in leader_lease (system DB). Multi-pod deploys elect one holder per name.
leaderLeases.empty: No leases held. Either the system is fresh or every cron has released its lease cleanly.

activeClaims.title: Active claims
activeClaims.subtitle: job_run rows currently in 'running' status. Stale heartbeats are reaped by LeaseManagerService.
activeClaims.empty: No active claims. The queue is empty or every worker just finished a cycle.

jobs.title: Job runs
jobs.subtitle: Long-running operator jobs (dreams / compaction / calibration refit / reindex / changefeed drain). SSE-streamed transitions; per-job drill shows progress / result / error.
jobs.sseHint: live SSE on accepted job_run transitions

maintenance.title: Maintenance cockpit
maintenance.subtitle: Scheduled jobs + manual triggers. Each card shows the last persisted run (via job_run + SchedulerRegistry), next-fire ETA, and a Run now button that delegates to the same code path the cron uses.

compaction.title: Compaction (hot → warm tier)
compaction.description: 03:17 UTC — facts past retention move to warm tier, optional LLM summary.

calibration_refit.title: Calibration refit (isotonic)
calibration_refit.description: 03:51 UTC — refit isotonic map from last-30d retraction outcomes. The same trigger also kicks source-trust refit.

source_trust_refit.title: Source-trust refit
source_trust_refit.description: 03:42 UTC — upserts source_trust(rate, sampleCount). Bundled with the calibration-refit trigger above.

reindex_embeddings.title: Reindex embeddings
reindex_embeddings.description: No cron — re-embed knowledge_fact across all tenants. Run after EMBEDDER_PROVIDER swap or model dimension change.

changefeed_drain.title: Changefeed drain → audit_event
changefeed_drain.description: Every minute — SHOW CHANGES per source, write audit_event, advance cursor.

maintenance.noRecentJobs: No persisted job runs yet. Trigger one above or wait for the next cron tick.

packs.title: Domain packs
packs.subtitle: Per-tenant pack installs: seed predicates, run eval fixtures, uninstall (predicates get deprecated, recorded facts survive). Builtin packs are seeded globally at boot.

installed.title: Installed
installed.subtitle: Packs installed into this tenant.
installed.empty: No packs installed in this tenant yet.
installed.uninstallPrompt: Uninstall "{packId}" — its predicates get deprecated (recorded facts survive). Type the pack id to confirm.

available.title: Available builtin packs
available.subtitle: Bundled with the service and seeded globally — already active for every tenant, nothing to install.

eval.title: Eval fixtures — {packId}
eval.throttleHint: Runs the live extractor (LLM calls) — throttled to 3 runs per minute.

install.fromRegistrySubtitle: Resolve a pack from the global registry and install it into this tenant (checksum-pinned).
install.manifestSubtitle: Paste a full pack manifest JSON — for packs distributed outside the registry.
install.checksumHint: optional — install fails when the computed checksum differs

acceptMcpTools.title: Pack declares MCP tools
acceptMcpTools.note: Installing changes this tenant's agent surface; external tools cause signed outbound calls to the publisher's endpoint. Review the declaration:

acceptModalities.title: Pack declares media modalities
acceptModalities.note: The pack asks to receive raw evidence (images, audio, documents) and to run processors over it. Review the declaration:

acceptSources.title: Pack declares sources
acceptSources.note: The pack names external systems the brain may READ through a connection (folders, buckets, sites, MCP servers). Nothing is read until an operator connects one. Review the declaration:

payment.title: Payment required
payment.opened: Checkout opened in a new tab.
payment.retryNote: After payment completes, retry the install — the entitlement is checked on every attempt.

success.title: Installed {packId} v{version}
success.webhookNote: Store it now: this HMAC secret signs indexer pushes and external MCP tool calls. It will NOT be shown again.

connections.title: Connections
connections.subtitle: The source plane: where the brain reads existing evidence from. A connection instantiates one `sources` entry of an installed pack — folders, buckets, sites, MCP servers — catalogues what is there, fetches what changed and commits it through the ordinary doors with a revision on every fact.

off.title: Source plane is off
off.body: This deployment answers 404 on /v1/admin/source-connections. Set SOURCE_PLANE_ENABLED=1 (and SOURCE_KIND_<KIND>=1 per connector) and restart; the scheduler registers at boot.

fences.title: Deployment fences
fences.fsRootsNone: none — SOURCE_FS_ROOTS unset, no directory may be read
fences.egressOn: operator opt-in on (SOURCE_EGRESS_ALLOW_PRIVATE) — a connection still needs config.allowPrivate
fences.egressOff: public hosts only (loopback / private / link-local refused)

list.title: Connected
list.subtitle: Connections in this tenant. Sync enqueues a job; Full re-walks everything and marks what is missing gone.
list.empty: No connections yet — pick a source from the catalogue below.
list.deletePrompt: Delete connection "{label}" — its catalogue is dropped, the documents and facts it committed stay. Type the label to confirm.
list.alreadyQueued: A sync for this connection is already queued ({runId}).

detail.title: Connection
detail.runInlineHint: Runs the sync in this request and shows the counters — for watching a first sync of a small source.
detail.sourceUnknown: the pack no longer declares this source

items.title: Catalogue
items.subtitle: What the connection has seen at the source ({total} items).
items.empty: Nothing catalogued yet — run a sync.

catalog.title: Connect a source
catalog.subtitle: What the packs installed here can read. Pick what you have; the brain asks the rest.
catalog.notAccepted: sources not accepted — reinstall the pack with acceptSources
catalog.empty: No pack in this tenant declares sources. Install file_memory or web_memory from Packs (accept modalities + sources).

availabilityHint.ready: the connector is installed and on
availabilityHint.missing: this build ships no such connector
availabilityHint.agent: runs on a local agent (brain-agent) — Connect asks for the agent id
availabilityHint.external: the publisher pushes through the doors; the connection is only the identity pushes are attributed to

create.title: Connect: {title}
create.created: Connected {label}. Run Sync to catalogue it.

stats.title: Produced
stats.hint: Catalogue rows by state and the facts this connection grounds (source.meta.source_connection). Stale = the source moved past the revision a fact was read at; closed = the delete policy ended it.
stats.factsUnknown: too many to count in time

runs.title: Runs
runs.subtitle: Every sync of this connection — queued, inline and agent runs alike, each a source_sync job.

headers.counters: seen · new · changed · gone · fetched · ingested · failed · closed

runs.notPersisted: JOB_RUN_PERSIST is off — runs leave no history.

item.title: Item
item.openHint: click a row to follow it to its document, asset and facts
item.documentsNone: no document yet — the item was not fetched, or a processor still has to extract its text
item.representationsNone: none yet — no processor has run over this asset (EVIDENCE_PROCESSOR_BROKER, and a pack that names the modality)
item.factsTruncated: more facts than shown — open the entity to see the rest
item.driftHint: read at an older revision than the catalogue now holds — the drift sweep marks it stale on its next pass

agents.title: Local agents
agents.subtitle: Connections that run on an agent — a laptop, a CI runner, a machine in the LAN. The brain keeps the books; the agent walks the source and posts what changed.
agents.setup: Run the agent on that machine
agents.setupHint: Install once; the service syncs every 5 minutes and survives reboots. Needs Node 20+ and, for repositories, git.
agents.none: No agent-host connections. Pick a source with availability "local agent" in the catalogue, or choose "local agent" when connecting.
agents.installHint: Install with a key: press "New key" — the command comes back with the key filled in.

modal.title: Agent {agentId}
modal.agentIdHint: How the brain will know this machine; the connections you point at it use this id.
modal.rootsHint: Optional ':'-separated allowlist for the folder connector on that machine (BRAIN_AGENT_ROOTS); empty = anything the user can read.
modal.keyExplain: Issues a brain:write key of this tenant labelled agent:<id> — a write key, never an admin one. You will see it once.
modal.keyOnce: This key is shown once. Run the command on the agent's machine now, or copy it somewhere safe.
modal.install: On a laptop or a server — as a service
modal.installHint: Saves the config (owner-only) and registers a launchd agent on macOS / a systemd user unit on Linux; it syncs every 5 minutes. brain-agent status / doctor / uninstall afterwards.
modal.ciHint: No file is written; the key rides in the environment. Exit 2 when a connection failed.
modal.keyRecord: Key {name} ({prefix}…) — revoke it under Key Lens if the machine is gone.

form.jsonHint: The exact config the brain receives. Editing here overrides the form.
form.noForm: This build has no form for the "{connector}" connector yet — fill the config as JSON.

host.serverBody: The brain reads the source itself: a mounted volume, a bucket, a site, an MCP server it can reach.
host.agentBody: A brain-agent on a laptop, a CI runner or a machine in the LAN walks the source there and posts what changed; the brain keeps the books.
host.serverOnly: This source runs on the brain.
host.agentOnly: This source runs on a local agent only.

form.agentIdHint: The id the agent runs with (BRAIN_AGENT_ID / --agent; default: its hostname). You get the run command after connecting.
form.label: Name
form.labelHint: How this connection shows up here; defaults to pack/source.
form.external: The publisher pushes through the doors; this connection is only the identity pushes are attributed to. Nothing to configure.
form.stdio: The agent spawns the pack's server:
form.pinnedUrlHint: pinned by the pack — the brain reads it, the operator cannot change it
form.installSecret: The brain authenticates with the pack's install secret; nothing to enter.
form.oauth: This server needs an OAuth sign-in — not available yet.

credential.title: Credential
credential.pairHint: Leave both empty to use the brain's own credential chain (env / instance role).
credential.accountHint: The brain reads the source as this account; its tokens stay encrypted on the brain.
credential.popupBlocked: The sign-in window was blocked — allow popups for this site and try again.
credential.notConfigured: This brain has no {provider} app registered — set {flag} (and the redirect URI below) on the brain.
credential.keyMissing: The brain has no SOURCE_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY — tokens are never stored in the clear, so no account can be connected until it is set.
credential.scopesShort: This account was connected with narrower permissions; connect it again.
credential.tokenHint: Pasted once, stored encrypted; a connected account is preferred where the CRM offers one.

errors.credential: a credential is needed for this auth

root.label: Folder
root.hint: Absolute path on the brain host.

rootAgent.label: Folder
rootAgent.hint: Absolute path on the agent's machine (inside BRAIN_AGENT_ROOTS if the agent sets it).

include.label: Only these paths
include.hint: gitignore-style, one per line, relative to the folder: docs/** — everything under docs; notes/2026 — that folder; *.md — every markdown file at any depth; /README.md — the root's only. Empty = the whole folder.

exclude.label: Skip these paths
exclude.hint: Same dialect: docs/archive — that folder; drafts/ — any folder named drafts; *.log — every log file. Applied after "only these".

extensions.label: Extensions
extensions.hint: Comma-separated, no dots; empty = the shape's defaults.

ignoreFiles.label: Ignore files honoured in the tree
ignoreFiles.hint: The machine's owner can leave a .brainignore (gitignore syntax, nested files allowed) anywhere under the folder to keep things out without touching this connection. Add .gitignore to also skip what git skips.

excludeDirs.label: Skip directories
excludeDirs.hint: Directory names skipped anywhere in the tree.

urls.label: Pages
urls.hint: One URL per line — read as they are.

sitemaps.label: Sitemaps
sitemaps.hint: One per line; every page they list is read (indexes followed one level).

sameHostOnly.label: Same host only
sameHostOnly.hint: Ignore sitemap entries on other hosts.

authHeader.label: Header name
authHeader.hint: The header the token is sent in.

ignoreRobots.label: Ignore robots.txt
ignoreRobots.hint: Only for a site you operate.

allowPrivate.label: Allow private hosts
allowPrivate.hint: Loopback / LAN addresses — the deployment already opted in.

endpoint.label: Endpoint
endpoint.hint: For MinIO / R2 / B2; empty = AWS.

allowPrivate.label: Allow a private endpoint
allowPrivate.hint: Loopback / LAN addresses — the deployment already opted in.

uriPrefixes.label: Resource URI prefixes
uriPrefixes.hint: Keep only resources whose URI starts with one of these; empty = all.

allowPrivate.label: Allow a private host
allowPrivate.hint: Loopback / LAN addresses — the deployment already opted in.

repo.label: Repository
repo.hint: Absolute path on the agent's machine (a clone, or the CI checkout).

ref.label: Ref
ref.hint: Branch, tag or commit; empty = HEAD.

include.label: Include
include.hint: One prefix or glob per line (docs/**, README.md, adr/????-*.md); empty = everything.

folderId.label: Folder
folderId.hint: A folder id from its URL, or root — My Drive. Everything beneath it.

includeShared.label: Also what is shared with me

driveId.label: Shared drive id
driveId.hint: Read a shared drive instead of My Drive.

extensions.label: Extensions
extensions.hint: Comma-separated, no dots; empty = the shape's defaults. Google Docs / Sheets / Slides are always taken.

folderPath.label: Folder
folderPath.hint: Path under the drive root, e.g. /Documents/Team; empty = the whole drive.

siteId.label: SharePoint site id
siteId.hint: Read a site's default document library instead of the account's OneDrive.

driveId.label: Drive id
driveId.hint: A specific drive (a group's, a colleague's).

extensions.label: Extensions
extensions.hint: Comma-separated, no dots; empty = the shape's defaults.

extensions.label: Extensions
extensions.hint: Comma-separated, no dots; empty = the shape's defaults.

apiDomain.label: API domain
apiDomain.hint: The api_domain of the account (https://<company>.pipedrive.com); empty = api.pipedrive.com.

15m.title: Every 15 minutes
15m.body: For sources that change all day.

text.title: Content
text.body: Fetch every changed item and commit it through the doors — facts, documents, evidence.

bytes.title: Content
bytes.body: Fetch the bytes into the evidence plane; processors extract the text.

manifest.title: Catalogue only
manifest.body: Record what exists and when it changed; fetch nothing.

close.title: Close
close.body: Its facts stay as history with an end date (recommended).

keep.title: Keep
keep.body: Nothing changes; the facts stay current.

retract.title: Retract
retract.body: Like close today; a full retraction cascade comes later.

form.fetchBudgetHint: Max items fetched per sync; empty = no cap.
form.ownerUserIdHint: Set = a personal connection: every row it writes is fenced to that user.
form.verticalHint: contextRef.vertical on every fact this connection writes; defaults to the pack.

folder.title: Folder
folder.body: A directory of documents — markdown, text, code, PDFs, Word / Excel / PowerPoint, mail. On the brain's host, or on a laptop through the local agent.

shapes.documentHint: markdown, text, csv, json, yaml, html, code
shapes.binaryHint: PDFs, Word / Excel / PowerPoint, .eml mail, images

site.title: Website
site.body: Pages and sitemaps of a docs portal, a wiki, a company site — read as text; PDFs and office documents handed to the evidence plane.

shapes.documentHint: HTML reduced to text, plain text, JSON
shapes.binaryHint: PDFs and office documents the sitemap lists

bucket.title: S3 bucket
bucket.body: Objects under a prefix of an S3 or S3-compatible bucket (AWS, MinIO, R2, B2).

shapes.documentHint: markdown, text, csv, json, yaml, html

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.body: The resources an MCP server exposes — a wiki, a knowledge base, a CMS behind an MCP endpoint.

repo.title: Git repository
repo.body: The committed docs of a repository — README, docs/**, ADRs, changelogs — read on the machine that has the clone, with the commit as the revision.

gdrive.title: Google Drive
gdrive.body: My Drive, a folder or a shared drive of a Google account you connect — read as documents, incrementally through the Drive changes feed.

shapes.documentHint: markdown, text, csv, json, html; Docs / Sheets / Slides as text

onedrive.title: OneDrive / SharePoint
onedrive.body: A OneDrive folder or a SharePoint document library of a Microsoft account you connect — incrementally through the Graph delta.

shapes.binaryHint: PDFs, Word / Excel / PowerPoint, mail, images

dropbox.title: Dropbox
dropbox.body: A Dropbox folder of an account you connect — incrementally through the folder cursor.

shapes.binaryHint: PDFs, Word / Excel / PowerPoint, mail, images

records.title: CRM · {connector}
records.body: People, organizations and deals of a CRM as facts with the revision they were read at — stage, amount, owner, title, company. Records enter deterministically: no model reads them.

external.title: Pushed by a publisher
external.body: An indexer or tool pushes here through the doors; connecting only creates the identity its writes are attributed to.

kinds.bothHint: two connections over the same place — one for documents, one for files

statusHint.agent: Runs on a brain-agent on the machine that has it; you get the command after connecting.
statusHint.disabled: Set {flag}=1 on the brain and restart.
statusHint.missing: This build ships no such connector.
statusHint.oauthUnconfigured: Register a {provider} app on the brain first ({flag}); the connect button then signs in.

picker.title: Pick the folder
picker.serverHint: The brain's own disk, inside SOURCE_FS_ROOTS. Open a folder to look inside; "use this" makes it the connection's folder; tick subfolders to read only those.
picker.agentHint: What agent {agentId} reported on its last check-in — the folders under its roots, names only. "Use this" makes one the connection's folder; tick subfolders to read only those.
picker.agentMissing: Agent {agentId} has not checked in yet. Install it on that machine (Local agents → Set up an agent) and wait one pass, or type the path.
picker.truncated: Only the first 500 subfolders are shown.
picker.tickHint: read only this subfolder (adds it to "only these paths")

accounts.title: Connected accounts
accounts.subtitle: Accounts the brain reads cloud sources as — connected once, tokens encrypted on the brain, refreshed before every sync.
accounts.none: No accounts connected. You connect one while adding a Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox source.

memoryLayers.title: The latest answer is not the whole memory.
memoryLayers.subtitle: Brain keeps the fact, the context around it and the source it came from as separate things: what was recorded, what happened, and what the system derives from them.

items.label: Facts & beliefs
items.title: Keep track of what changes
items.desc: Typed facts keep their history and unresolved conflicts. Derived beliefs track revisions and the scenes supporting them.

items.label: Episodes & scenes
items.title: Keep the surrounding context
items.desc: Source episodes retain the original conversation. Scenes capture events and state changes, so a short memory can lead back to a fuller account.

items.label: Sources & evidence
items.title: Make the answer inspectable
items.desc: Provenance links memory to its sources. Evidence fragments can point to a text passage, page region or time range in an external asset.

memoryLayers.note: Scene, belief and evidence capabilities depend on the enabled server configuration and domain packs. Media registration stores references and metadata; processing requires a configured processor.

architecture.title: Every answer can be walked back to where it came from.
architecture.subtitle: Brain separates source material, derived memory and retrieval. The graph gives memory structure; source links keep that structure inspectable.

stages.title: Capture & resolve
stages.desc: Conversations and documents enter through REST or MCP. Indexers propose candidates; identity and conflict resolution decide what becomes a fact.

stages.title: Build connected memory
stages.desc: SurrealDB holds entities, relationships and temporal facts alongside source episodes and derived scenes and beliefs. Evidence links connect memory to its supporting material.

stages.title: Retrieve & verify
stages.desc: Semantic and lexical search find candidates. Graph walks and multi-hop add context. Synthesis cites evidence; strict verification can abstain when support is missing.

architecture.packBridge: Domain Packs shape vocabulary, extraction and memory models throughout this path.

details.title: Rebuildable memory
details.desc: Derived worlds can be rebuilt from retained episodes in a staged version, then promoted while reads stay pinned to the previous world until the switch.

details.title: One engine, different profiles
details.desc: Retrieval profiles configure the trade-offs for different kinds of conversations. The NestJS service can run API and background workers together or as separate roles.

domainPacks.title: Domain Packs. Your domain, your memory model.
domainPacks.subtitle: Give Brain the vocabulary and lifecycles of your product. A versioned pack extends the shared engine without a fork: from what to extract to how events, states and evidence are represented.

capabilities.title: Typed vocabulary
capabilities.desc: Predicates, value types, conflict semantics and PII classes.

capabilities.title: Domain-specific extraction
capabilities.desc: Instructions, examples, indexers and evaluation fixtures for your source material.

capabilities.title: A model of what changes
capabilities.desc: Scene schemas, state transitions, attention hints, verification rules and retention hints.

capabilities.title: Tools for the agent
capabilities.desc: Optional pack MCP tools, activated with operator consent.

problem.title: Every session starts from zero.
problem.subtitle: Not for lack of a capable model — nothing is keeping the record. The context that does survive is re-pasted by hand, locked inside one vendor's client, or arrives with no way to check it.

items.label: Re-explained
items.title: Context you pay for twice
items.desc: Decisions, constraints and prior work go back into the prompt every session, or they are lost. The work of establishing context is repeated on every run, at full token price.

items.label: Trapped
items.title: Memory that stops at the client
items.desc: Built-in memory belongs to the client holding it. What one assistant learned does not reach the next, and there is rarely a way to take it with you.

items.label: Unverifiable
items.title: Recall you cannot check
items.desc: A remembered claim with no source and no date cannot be verified. Nothing says whether it still holds, where it came from, or what it replaced.

sharedGraph.title: The memory belongs to you, not to the client.
sharedGraph.subtitle: Connect Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor and your own code to the same graph. What one of them writes, the next one recalls — because the workspace comes from the key, not from the app that happens to be open.

facts.title: Scope comes from the key
facts.desc: The workspace, the tools and the reach of every call are resolved from the API key. Nothing to configure per client, nothing to keep in sync.

facts.title: The same graph either way
facts.desc: Self-hosted, it is a SurrealDB you run. Managed, it is the same schema and the same API behind brain.inite.ai.

facts.title: The record is portable
facts.desc: Source episodes are retained, not just the conclusions drawn from them — and the derived memory can be rebuilt from those episodes.

sharedGraph.note: Which tools a client sees depends on the key's scopes and installed packs. Episodes are retained and stream out as NDJSON over the API by default — a self-hosted deployment can switch either off.

plainly.title: What is true about Brain, stated flatly.
plainly.subtitle: The claims worth checking before you connect anything, without the adjectives.

items.title: It sits between a vector store and a knowledge platform
items.desc: More structure than embeddings in a table: typed facts, entities, time and provenance. Less ceremony than a platform that asks you to model the domain before it stores a sentence.

items.title: It is not an agent framework
items.desc: Brain stores, resolves and retrieves. It does not run your loop, own your prompts or choose your model. The agent stays yours.

items.title: Self-hosted, the data is in a database you run
items.desc: The memory is a SurrealDB you operate, and nothing has to be requested from us to read it. Traffic leaves your network only for the model providers you configure.

items.title: AGPL-3.0-or-later, hosted service included
items.desc: Everything running brain.inite.ai is in the repository. Network copyleft is a real obligation, not a badge: changes you serve over a network stay open.

items.title: Published numbers come with their protocol
items.desc: Every result names its dataset, model, baseline and run configuration, and describes those runs rather than your deployment. A number without a protocol is marketing.

items.title: Capabilities are per-tenant runtime configuration
items.desc: What is on for one workspace is not silently on for another, and changes take effect without a redeploy. Several capabilities ship off until an operator turns them on.
